nodes.title: Child-session execution: the orchestrator hands a plan to a cheaper child process
Overlap check misses rewritten rule copies with no H2 headings
rules --project resolves against the process cwd, not the repo root
Rules pruning uses the sk- prefix where the design specified a manifest
The EPIC move and the retirement left 30 broken relative links in docs/
Nothing gates the freshness of the committed plugin/bin/sidekick bundle
The paths: spike was never run, and two documents state its unverified answer as fact
rules check exit codes are undocumented and conflate drift with failure for hooks and CI
The plugin has no PM seat: no board discovery, no tested mechanics, no gh minimum
A repo can't be brought under tracking without hand-building the board, statuses, views, and labels
Nothing derives what to pick up at session start; pointers end up in memory files
Filing and closing are ad hoc: issues arrive in bursts, close comments lack evidence, no learning record exists
Milestones have no stated outcome, no entry gate, and no close audit — scope creeps and the backlog balloons
The Verify column is named but never defined; the verification-moves-to-use ruling lives only in memory
sk-typescript's no-bypass and runtime-schema rules have no answer for guard-narrowed values or a CLI parsing its own tool's output
Assertions written against whatever the fixture contains pass under wrong code; nothing asks what a test would catch
Whether claude plugin eval can reach api.github.com is unverified, so no skill that calls gh can be eval-tested
sidekick pm discovers user-owned boards only; an organisation board reports no-board with no hint why
A design pass before brainstorming: the first extension to bring back after the pivot
Nothing sweeps the backlog or triages change requests, so stale issues and scope changes accumulate
Three execution modes exist and nothing says when each fits or what the review cycles cost
USAGE has no per-skill walkthrough, so the loop cannot be visualised end to end
The worker handoff requires a git worktree; a plain branch in the main checkout should be an option
sk-language's sentence limit does not say how a code span counts, so two reviewers count the same sentence differently
sk-milestone writes the learning record after the tag, so the release cannot carry it
The plugin install leaves the flat install's hooks in a consumer's settings.local.json, so every Stop runs a missing binary
The execution process for a milestone: what R6 measured and what changes before the next plan is dispatched
Issues, milestones, and docs have no standard format; the stated shapes live in skill prose and practice drifts from them
Nothing marks an issue as untriaged, so one filed without a disposition is never triaged
GitHub's native labels go unused: no issue is tagged bug or enhancement, and the conventions leave no room for them
sidekick pm reads the board's item list, which left out new cards for over 45 minutes, so pickup and lint missed four issues
sk-milestone caps a milestone at two sessions; the session-sized unit is the execution plan, not the release
The rules name GitHub's eventual consistency for one case only, so a lagging list gets read as the truth
Code comments run long despite sk-clean-code's one-line default, and nothing checks them
AGENTS.md's rules install step runs the released plugin binary, so a rule edit in this repo is never installed
sk-design's triggering is checked only by use; a claude plugin eval suite would measure when it fires and when it stays quiet
The ADR index stops at ADR-0005 and still describes the harness
Review-cycle measurements are summed by hand from transcripts, and the method has no home
Installing rules from the repo bundle puts unreleased sidekick rules into every repo on the machine
Every milestone waits on the operator at each pause in the loop; nothing says which pauses an agent could hold
The pickup brief knows nothing of a milestone's plans: next says pull one, and the Plans clause never shows
sk-design proposes options before asking what the operator values, so a note can design against a goal nobody holds
An unscoped claude plugin update targets a stale project-scope record, so the release step leaves the user install behind
The sk-* rules say nothing about precedence against a repo's own rules, so a conflict in an external project has no fix
A --project rules install ships sk-pm-conventions into repos sidekick doesn't track, with no way to leave it out
A context monitor hook: warn the model before the context window fills, as GSD's does
sk-design's explore scale has no path to adopt an exploration written elsewhere
A hand-built board passes `sidekick pm board`; nothing checks its workflows and views against the reference
`sidekick rules check --project` reports `[missing]` and exits 2 when the rules are delivered at user level
`sk-track` forbids filing loose, not-deferred work, the state `sk-orient` reads as tier 2
The `sidekick` skill says only a copied board gets the Focus filter; the API sets it
Plans must put operator steps before Task 1, because superpowers appends trailing sections to the last task
`sidekick pm lint`'s `unboarded` check only sees open issues
`sk-track` issue bodies state measured claims without the command that produced them
`sk-worker`'s scan cannot dry-run a plan that edits one file several times with its writes stubbed
`sk-agent-prompts.md`'s `agents/**` path loads it on every file under any `agents/` folder
Plan preparation leaves output-producing commands without an Expected, so the scan skips them
`sk-execute` says to fast-forward the base branch; `sk-track` and PR-based repos close through `Closes #N`
Sidekick's docs taxonomy omits where research done inside a design lives; sk-design's explore scale puts it beside design.md
The plan scan tests the plan against itself; add a check of each new claim against its source and of every copy of a fixed fact
sk-execute's reviewer rule never reaches a subagent-driven reviewer; superpowers filters process rules out of the constraints slot
sk-agent-prompts.md prescribes older-model scaffolds: reasoning in prose, a scripted framing pass, and a Rule 3 heading that contradicts its intent
Two pairs of sk-* rules give different instructions for the same moment: labelling uncertainty, and a problem outside the task
sk-worker's 'commit once per task' and sk-design's patterns stance contradict superpowers without naming the override
sk-milestone and sk-track carry the sidekick repo's own release facts into every consumer repo
pm lint's Revisit when: marker rejects the bold label form that issue bodies use
sk-execute has no mode for plans whose writes are public GitHub operations
Managed boards have no Plan field, so a milestone's plans show only in its description
Long code comments are caught only by a reviewer's judgment; no check flags them
Board #2's short description still names milestones R1-R3 and the pre-plugin rules path
Plans are parsed out of the milestone description's prose; they need a delimited header
pickup's active milestone is the earliest due, not the one being worked in
An In Progress card's age counts from its issue's last update, so a card move does not reset it
sidekick pm ignores flags it does not recognise, so a mistyped flag runs as if it were absent
Plans script the executor instead of trusting it; plan code should be intent, and the executor should reason past small misfits
